title: Operator sidecar for ephemeral admin utilities and safe one-off scripts
creator: Maya R. Patel
description: Motivation: On-call engineers and SREs need a safer, auditable way to run one-off admin scripts and short-lived utilities against customer-facing control planes (hosted and dedicated) without granting long-lived elevated credentials or requiring full runbook execution. This ticket proposes an Operator-sidecar pattern: a small, sandboxed service that attaches to operator/controller pods and executes verified admin tasks under strict policies (time-limited tokens, network egress restrictions, resource quotas, mandatory dry-run, and built-in audit events). The sidecar is intended to replace ad-hoc SSH/runbook shells and reduce blast radius while preserving operator ergonomics.
acceptance_criteria: Sidecar runs as an opt-in container injected into operator/controller deployments and can be toggled via a label (redwood.io/ephemeral-admin: enabled)
Admin actions are executed through signed, expiring tokens issued by the control plane; tokens default to 5-minute TTL and scope-limited via RBAC policies
Every invocation emits an audit event to the platform audit log (requester, cmd, args, target path, dry-run flag, exit code), and an entry is visible in Console activity feed within 30s
Safe mode: commands must pass a whitelist/regexp policy and cannot touch production data directories or escalate privileges (no setuid, no kernel sysctl changes)
Dry-run is the default; any write-capable command requires an explicit two-step confirmation (create token with reason + acknowledge) recorded in the audit trail
End-to-end integration tests cover happy path, denied-command path, token expiry, and audit emission; CI gating must pass
Latency/overhead: sidecar container memory < 80MB baseline, cold-start < 800ms for an injected pod, and CPU bounded via cgroup to prevent noisy-neighbor impact
Security review completed and documented in Confluence; automatic revocation workflow exists for compromised tokens
design_notes: We prefer an internal HTTP/2 gRPC-lite endpoint that operator pod can call; avoids SSH and leverages existing mTLS in the control plane
Container is intentionally minimal: busybox-derived runtime with a small Go binary for policy enforcement and execution sandboxing
Use seccomp + unprivileged user namespaces where available; fall back to policy-only mode on unsupported clusters with explicit warning
Audit events reuse our existing audit schema (audit.v2) so Console and SIEM integrations can consume without adapter work
RBAC binding model mirrors control plane roles; use the same LDAP/SCIM groups to avoid extra sync layers
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (spike): PoC sidecar binary that accepts a signed token, validates against local policy, runs a restricted command in a timeout'd sandbox (1 week)
Phase 2 (integration): Hook token issuance into Admin Console, add UI flow for two-step confirmation and reason, wire audit events (2 weeks)
Phase 3 (hardening): seccomp profiles, e2e tests, resource limits, performance tuning (1 week)
Phase 4 (rollout): Canary in staging -> limited production tenants -> broader rollout with monitoring and rollback plan (2 sprints)
Deliverables: sidecar image, helm/manifest toggles, Console action page, integration tests, security review doc
safety_checks: Whitelist-based command validator with denylist patterns (no direct DB dumps, no private key exposures)
Execution timeouts and kill-by-OOM/cgroup limits enforced
Dry-run default and explicit verification step for writes
Audit-first model: reject any execution if audit pipeline is unreachable
Automatic token revocation endpoint and manual emergency revoke via Console
telemetry_and_monitoring: Emit metrics: admin_invocations_total, admin_invocation_failures, avg_execution_time_ms, tokens_issued_total
SLO: failed_invocations_ratio < 0.5% in steady state; alert on increase
Trace: attach tracer span for each invocation that includes token_id and operator_pod_id
Dashboard: per-cluster and per-tenant invocation heatmap, top command types, and top callers
